newsitem.title: FINLAND: Cultor sees better 1997 overall prospects.
newsitem.headline: Cultor sees better 1997 overall prospects.

text.p: Finnish food and enzymes group Cultor Oy said on Wednesday overall 1997 prospects for the group are better than the outlook for full year 1996.
"It (the year 1997) looks better," Cultor CEO Bjorn Mattsson told a news conference when asked about the outlook for 1997.

Cultor said earlier its January-August profit after financial items fell to 196 million markka from 338 million in the first eight months of 1995, and that the group expects its full-year 1996 earnings per share to be "about one quarter lower" than the 14.91 markka of 1995.
Cultor's January-August EPS fell to 5.55 markka from 10.24.
"The year 1996 is a period of consolidation and large non-recurring costs, which are inputs for the future," Mattsson said.
Cultor said earlier its January-August gross investments rose to 1.6 billion markka from 378 million in the first eight months of 1995.

The most significant were the acquisition of Food Science Group from U.S. company Pfizer the start of xylose plant construction in Lenzing, Austria, and the acquisition of Solvay's enzyme operations for Genencor, it said.
Mattsson said he expected third tertial operating profit and net sales to rise clearly on the second tertial of 1996.
"We expect the third tertial to be clearly above the second tertial," he said.
Cultor's May-August net sales rose to 2.8 billion markka from 2.2 billion in the second tertial of 1995, but its second tertial operating profit fell to 211 million markka from 253 million.
Cultor said earlier its January-August net sales rose to 5.4 billion markka from 4.0 billion, but its eight-month operating profit fell to 301 million markka from 360 million.
